canon: Kell’s notebook records that Cob is wearing the boots and that their ownership is disputed.
A pigeon watched from the hoist beam, and a stone clanged against the hoist hook.
Cob accepted two silver crowns from Bartholomew and tucked them away.
Sir Bartholomew successfully climbed the hoist rope and reached the beam beside Prout.
From beside the body, Sir Bartholomew saw a second, narrow level mark on Prout’s neck beneath the noose mark, swelling beneath the hair at the back of his head, and clean palms.
Cob accepted two silver crowns from Sir Bartholomew and said he found the boots in the yard; he kept the boots on.
Kell recorded the two-crown payment and Cob’s answer in her notebook.

repairs.assessment: The player is enjoying a playful, grandiose entrance and banter with the yard’s occupants; the exchanges are moving naturally and Cob has already stopped throwing stones.
repairs.notes: Let this reach the player through the world: As Cob boasts about his boots, he stamps to punctuate it; the left one gives a faint papery crackle. Let the detail pass once without explaining it.
